newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up on slow farm sales, technical.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up on slow farm sales, technical.

text.p: Slow farmer selling, firm cash basis makets and signals the market was oversold boosted CBOT soybean futures to a higher close, traders said.
Reports that yields were declining as the U.S. harvest progressed also contributed to the advances, they said.
"There's a lack of bean movement. The guys are more interested in getting the beans out than in selling them," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co, of harvesting efforts.
Soybean combining gained speed over the weekend and forecasts for U.S. Midwest weather remain conducive for active soybean harvesting.
But many traders cited technical signals as central to the gains Tuesday in soybean futures.
"It's just short covering ahead of the report. There is a lot of evening up waiting for Friday morning," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
USDA at 0730 CDT Friday will release its October crop production and monthly supply/demand reports. Recent private crop estimates have pegged the crop at roughly 2.3 billion bushels.
Soybeans closed one to 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with November up 2-1/4 at $7.36-1/2 a bushel.
The nine day relative strength index (RSI) for November closed at 28.478 points, above the recent low of 17.374 set Friday but still below the benchmark oversold level of 30.
Demand for soybean futures was evenly divided between cash-connected commission houses, funds and locals amid the absence of a large player, the traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 40,000, down from 56,785 Monday.

Soybean futures and options trading was quiet with ADM Investor Services the key participant in options with a purchase of 1,500 January $7.25 calls and a sale of 1,500 January $7.50 calls at 11-1/2 to 12 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 25,000, down from 28,308 Monday.
